name: Oxycodone
description: Oxycodone (OxyContin, Percocet) facts: uses, risks, interactions, overdose signs, withdrawal timeline, and how to get it legally with a prescription in the US.
quick: Oxycodone is a strong prescription opioid used for pain severe enough to need an opioid when other treatments are not enough. It is sold alone (Roxicodone, OxyContin) and combined with acetaminophen (Percocet). It is a Schedule II controlled substance, and it carries a high risk of addiction, overdose, and withdrawal.
facts: OxyContin, Roxicodone, Oxaydo, Xtampza ER; with acetaminophen: Percocet
Pain severe enough to require an opioid, when alternatives are inadequate
Immediate-release tablets, capsules, and oral solution; extended-release tablets and capsules

blocks.p: Oxycodone is FDA-approved for pain severe enough to require an opioid and for which other treatments, such as non-opioid pain relievers, are inadequate. Extended-release forms such as OxyContin are only for severe, persistent pain that needs daily, around-the-clock opioid treatment over a long period.[[1]]

It works by activating mu-opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord, which reduces how pain signals are felt. The same receptors control breathing, which is why too much can stop a person breathing.
Combination products such as Percocet also contain acetaminophen, which has its own daily limit and can damage the liver in high doses.

The figures below come from the FDA-approved label and describe how prescribers typically use oxycodone. They are not personal dosing advice. A prescriber sets the dose for each person and adjusts it over time.[[1]]

blocks.p: The CDC recommends immediate-release opioids at the lowest effective dose for acute pain, usually for three days or less and rarely more than seven, and careful reassessment before any dose increase.[[2]]
Extended-release tablets must be swallowed whole. Crushing, chewing, or dissolving them releases a potentially fatal dose all at once.

sections.q: What are the risks and side effects of oxycodone?

boxed.title: FDA boxed warnings
items: Oxycodone exposes users to risks of addiction, misuse, and abuse, which can lead to overdose and death.
Life-threatening slowed breathing can occur, especially when starting treatment or after a dose increase.
Accidental ingestion, especially by children, can cause a fatal overdose.
Use with benzodiazepines or other central nervous system depressants, including alcohol, can cause profound sedation, slowed breathing, coma, and death.
Prolonged use during pregnancy can cause neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome, which may be life-threatening if not recognized and treated.
Drugs that block CYP3A4, or stopping drugs that speed it up, can raise oxycodone levels and cause a fatal overdose.

blocks.p: **Common side effects** include constipation, nausea, drowsiness, dizziness, itching, headache, dry mouth, and sweating.[[1]]

**Serious risks** include slowed or stopped breathing, severe low blood pressure, adrenal insufficiency, serotonin syndrome with some antidepressants, and increased sensitivity to pain (opioid-induced hyperalgesia).[[1]]

sections.q: What does oxycodone overdose look like?

blocks.p: Signs of an oxycodone overdose include pinpoint pupils, extreme sleepiness or inability to wake up, slow, shallow, or stopped breathing, gurgling or snoring sounds, limp body, and blue or gray lips and fingertips. Overdose risk is highest when oxycodone is combined with alcohol, benzodiazepines, or other sedatives, after a period without use, and with counterfeit pills.[[1]][[3]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, cannot be woken, has blue or gray lips, or is breathing slowly or not at all.
Give naloxone (Narcan or a generic nasal spray, sold without a prescription) into one nostril. If there is no response after 2 to 3 minutes, give another dose.
If you are trained, give rescue breaths. Otherwise place the person on their side so they do not choke.
Stay with them. Naloxone can wear off before oxycodone does, so the overdose can return even after the person wakes up.
Most states have Good Samaritan laws that protect people who call 911 for an overdose from some drug charges.

blocks.p: Anyone prescribed an opioid can keep naloxone at home. It is sold without a prescription at pharmacies, and many health departments give it free.[[3]]

sections.q: What is oxycodone withdrawal like, and how long does it last?

blocks.p: People who take oxycodone regularly for more than a few weeks become physically dependent, even when they take it exactly as prescribed. Dependence is not the same as addiction, but it means stopping suddenly causes withdrawal.[[1]]

timeline.title: Early symptoms
timeline.text: Anxiety, restlessness, yawning, sweating, runny nose, watery eyes, and muscle aches.

timeline.title: Peak withdrawal
timeline.text: Diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea and vomiting, goosebumps, dilated pupils, fast heartbeat, and strong cravings. Rarely dangerous in healthy adults, but dehydration can be serious.

timeline.title: Lingering symptoms
timeline.text: Poor sleep, low mood, low energy, and cravings can continue for weeks. Tolerance falls quickly, which raises the risk of overdose if use restarts.

blocks.warn: After a break, the body loses tolerance within days. Returning to a previous dose of oxycodone can cause a fatal overdose.

blocks.p: The FDA warns against stopping opioids abruptly in people who are physically dependent. A prescriber can taper the dose gradually, often by 10% or less per month for long-term users, and medicines such as clonidine or lofexidine can ease symptoms. For opioid use disorder, buprenorphine and methadone cut the risk of death roughly in half.[[2]]

sections.q: How do you get oxycodone legally in the US?

blocks.p: In the United States, oxycodone is a Schedule II controlled substance. The only legal way to get it is with a prescription from a clinician registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), filled by a licensed pharmacy. Depending on state law, that can be a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.[[4]]

ul: **Refills:** Schedule II prescriptions cannot be refilled. A prescriber can write several prescriptions at once, with dates when each may be filled, for up to a 90-day supply in total.[[5]]

**Telehealth:** federal flexibilities let DEA-registered clinicians prescribe Schedule II to V medicines after a telemedicine visit, without a prior in-person exam, through December 31, 2026. A permanent DEA rule was under final review in late 2026. State rules can be stricter.[[6]]
**Monitoring:** prescribers and pharmacists in most states check a prescription drug monitoring program, a database of controlled-substance prescriptions, before prescribing or dispensing.

**Pharmacies:** a legitimate pharmacy always requires a valid prescription, has a licensed pharmacist available, and is licensed in the state it ships to. The FDA's BeSafeRx tool and the NABP's safe pharmacy list help confirm a pharmacy is real.[[7]][[8]]
**Cost:** generic immediate-release oxycodone is inexpensive and covered by most plans; many plans require prior authorization for extended-release forms or high doses.
**Quantity limits:** many states and insurers limit first-time opioid prescriptions for acute pain to a 3- to 7-day supply.

blocks.warn: Pills sold as oxycodone, OxyContin, or "M30s" outside a pharmacy are often counterfeit. The DEA reports that fake pills frequently contain fentanyl or methamphetamine, and they cannot be told apart by appearance.[[9]]

blocks.p: **Traveling:** keep the medicine in its original pharmacy container and carry a copy of the prescription. Check the rules of the destination country before travel, because many countries restrict controlled medicines or require a permit.

Yes, but only with a valid prescription and only from a pharmacy licensed in your state. Many licensed pharmacies, including mail-order pharmacies run by insurers, fill oxycodone prescriptions online and ship them. Buying oxycodone from a website that does not require a prescription is illegal, and the product is often fake.[[7]][[9]]

blocks.p: **Signs that an online seller is illegal:**

ul: It sells oxycodone with no prescription, or after only a short online questionnaire.
It takes orders through social media, messaging apps, or email.
It asks for payment in cryptocurrency, gift cards, or money transfers.
It has no US street address, no state pharmacy license, and no pharmacist to speak to.
Its prices are far below those of ordinary pharmacies, or it ships from another country.

blocks.p: The FDA's BeSafeRx tool links to each state's license lookup, and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy lists verified online pharmacies.[[7]][[8]]

faq: How long does oxycodone take to work?
Immediate-release oxycodone usually starts to relieve pain within 10 to 30 minutes and peaks after about 1 hour. Extended-release forms work over 12 hours and are not meant for fast relief.
How long does oxycodone stay in your system?
Its half-life is about 3 to 4.5 hours, so most of a dose is cleared within a day. Urine tests can usually detect it for 1 to 3 days, and longer after regular use.
What is the difference between oxycodone and OxyContin?
OxyContin is a brand of extended-release oxycodone that lasts about 12 hours. Plain oxycodone tablets are immediate release and last 4 to 6 hours.
By weight, oxycodone is roughly 1.5 times as potent as hydrocodone by mouth. Both are Schedule II and carry the same boxed warnings.
Can you buy oxycodone online legally?
Only with a valid prescription, from a pharmacy licensed in your state. Sites that sell oxycodone without a prescription are illegal, and their pills are frequently counterfeit and contain fentanyl.
Is it safe to stop oxycodone suddenly?
After more than a few weeks of regular use, stopping suddenly causes withdrawal. A prescriber can plan a gradual taper.
